summary: José Canedo Grille (1902–1945) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Seminario Mayor de Santiago de Compostela, the University of Granada, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1936), later holding a post at Heidelberg University in 1943.

José Carlos Ribeiro Calazans Duarte works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at institutions including Sorbonne Nouvelle, EPHE, and Lusófona University (PhD 2006–2012), later serving as an Assistant Professor at Lusófona University from 2006 to 2021.

José Ignacio Cabezón (born 1956) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and UW–Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, later serving at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and UC Santa Barbara (from 2001).

José Ventura Traveset (1862–1941) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He held posts as Professor of Humanities at the University of Granada (1887–1889) and as Professor at the University of Valencia (appointed 1901).
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer (born 1974) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, and at Munich. She held positions at Munich (~2007–2012, 2017–2021) and became Professor at Leipzig in 2021.

Joy Brennan specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, Constance Furey, and traditional teacher Diane Martin.

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger (born 1952) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Goshen College (~1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1978–1984), and served as a professor at Emory University (~1992).

Joydeb Dinda works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (until 2022) and became an Assistant Professor at Laxmi Devi Shroff Adarsh Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya in 2022.

Jozef Deleu (1925–1994) was an Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Adriaan Scharpé and studied at Hamburg with Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf, later serving as docent in Indology at Ghent University (1964–1990).

João Carlos Barbosa Gonçalves specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He earned a PhD in linguistics at the University of São Paulo (2005–2009) and held professorships at the State University of Campinas (2003–2005) and São Paulo (2014–2015).

Juan Gelabert y Gordiola (1843–1894) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Francisco García Ayuso, earned a Ph.D. at Complutense University of Madrid (~1865–1868), and served there as Professor of Sanskrit from 1883 to 1894.
Juan Wu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök specializes in Indology. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III (from 2001) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2018).

Judith Simmer-Brown (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Cornell College, Florida State, Columbia, and Walden University (PhD ~1980–1985), and joined Naropa University in 1977 as a professor.

Judith Snodgrass is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA (1987) and PhD (1994) at the University of Sydney and served as Associate Professor at Western Sydney University from 1991 to 2016.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (2007). He held posts at the University of Michigan, including Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies (attested 2019).

Juhyung Rhi works in Buddhist studies, art history, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and has served as Professor of Art History at Seoul National University since 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe works in philosophy and other fields. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He was Professor of Greek and Latin philosophy at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and a member of the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques.
